transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we go any further with this supplier early-payment program, I want to make sure we've covered all our bases in the pre-authorization huddle. The draft proposal references the full $10 million submitted invoice pool, but I'm not seeing a quarterly cash cap, any guidance on accounting classification, or an invoice-exclusion control. I need procurement, treasury, and tax accounting to weigh in on these gaps before I can consider signing off. Let's walk through each one.

transcript.text: I confirmed with cash management this morning that only $4,500,000 can be used for early supplier payments during the quarter without drawing on the operating liquidity buffer. The program must carry an exact quarterly early-payment cap of $4,500,000.

transcript.text: I need to flag something important on the accounting classification gap. I received a tax-accounting memo yesterday stating that supplier discounts under this program must be recorded as finance costs rather than procurement expense, and that a quarterly finance-cost reconciliation will be required. The memo has not yet been attached to the approval file, so I want to make sure that's addressed before we move forward.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue with the invoice pool. While reviewing supplier contracts this week, I found $2,400,000 of invoices that are subject to public-procurement clauses prohibiting early-payment discounts. That means the eligible invoice pool is exactly $7,600,000, not $10,000,000, and those restricted invoices must be excluded by an invoice-exclusion control before any payments go out.
